subject: POC capacity planning — Acme AI (recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@acme-ai.com>, Priya Rao <priya@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: POC capacity planning — Acme AI (recap & next steps)

Thanks again for the call earlier, Samir and Priya — good alignment on goals. I wanted to capture the recap and proposed next steps so we have a single reference for the POC. Please flag anything I missed.

TL;DR (ask): Redwood to reserve a baseline pool of 2x A100 GPUs for Acme's POC (us-west-2). Autoscale policy to allow bursts up to 6 GPUs for short windows. Confirm acceptance by EOD Thu so we can provision.

Success criteria (what Acme will evaluate):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for 512-token request profiles under steady load
- Throughput: sustained 50 QPS with 95% of requests within latency SLO
- Cost per 1M tokens under POC within the budget we discussed (~$Xk/month est)
- Functional: model outputs meet quality bar on your eval set (we'll run A/B with current infra)

Evaluation plan & timelines (proposed, 6-week POC):
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, credentials & network setup, sample dataset ingestion
- Week 1: integration + sanity tests (endpoints, auth, example prompts)
- Week 2: load validation (scale/throughput tests, KV/prefix cache enabled)
- Week 3: feature testing (tooling, streaming, function-calls if used)
- Week 4: end-to-end runs & quality evals (your eval set + human spot checks)
- Week 5: optimization pass (batching/quantization suggestions, model variant testing)
- Week 6: decision window & handoff (SOW/signing if moving to Dedicated)

Capacity ask (detailed):
- Reserved baseline: 2x A100 (guaranteed) in us-west-2 for the POC duration
- Autoscale: scale up to 6 GPUs for burst traffic; warm-pool of 1-2 instances to reduce cold-starts
- Burst expectations: short bursts (5-15 minutes) to handle 2-3x traffic spikes; we will enforce a 10-minute cooldown between bursts to protect capacity
- KV/prefix cache: enabled by default to reduce token cost for repeated prefixes

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (sales owner) and Dylan (infra lead)
- Acme: Samir (platform lead) and Priya (ML lead)

Next steps (action items):
1) Acme: confirm reservation & burst ceiling (reply-all) — Samir/Priya
2) Acme: provide sample traffic profile and representative prompt set (S3 link or samples) — Priya
3) Redwood: send SOW + provisional cost estimate and schedule provisioning when confirmed — Marissa
4) Redwood infra: prepare reserved pool and autoscale config; provide VPC peering/IP ranges if needed — Dylan/Dev
5) Schedule a 30m kickoff once network details are in place (proposed Wed 07/14 10am PT)

Attachments: acme-poc-capacity-plan.xlsx (capacity table + cost est) and provisional SOW (attached).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Samir Shah <samir@acme-ai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priya Rao <priya@acme-ai@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC capacity planning — Acme AI (recap & next steps)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming high-level acceptance; a few clarifications before we lock the reservation: 

1) Baseline vs burst: can we limit sustained autoscale to 4 GPUs and allow 6 only for very short bursts? Our internal cost controls prefer a hard cap of 4 sustained GPUs.
2) Warm pool: a single warm instance is okay, but can you describe expected cold-start times if warm pool is exhausted?
3) Cost: can you share a ballpark hourly rate or a delta between reserved 2x vs autoscaled GPU usage so we can pre-approve budget?
4) Network: we need the exact IP ranges and VPC peering guide — we can only accept peering if it meets our egress policies (no public IPs on the inference endpoints).

Also attaching our sample traffic profile in a follow-up email — Priya will send the payload samples. If we can get the SOW and a simple cost model today, we can confirm by Thu.

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Platform Engineering
Acme AI
samir@acme-ai.com

Subject: Re: POC capacity planning — Acme AI (recap & next steps)

Samir — appreciate the quick turnaround. Answers inline below and updated ask.

1) Baseline vs burst
- We can make sustained autoscale soft-cap at 4 GPUs and allow 6 GPUs for emergency bursts. The autoscaler policy will prefer staying at <=4 unless queue/latency thresholds force an additional node.

2) Cold-starts
- With a warm pool of 1-2 instances, typical cold-start for a new GPU worker is ~45-90s for model load on our optimized runtime (depends on model variant). For your 6-GPU bursts, if warm pool is 1, worst-case ~90s for the last node; with 2 warm instances it's closer to ~45s. We can prioritize keeping the KV cache primed for the baseline nodes to reduce effective latency.

3) Cost model (ballpark)
- Reserved baseline (2x A100): $XX/hr (reserved rate)
- Autoscale extra GPUs (on-demand): $YY/hr per GPU
- For the POC window we estimate $Zk-$Wk total depending on burst usage — detailed numbers in the attached SOW and the attached acme-poc-capacity-plan.xlsx.

4) Network/VPC
- Dylan/Dev will share exact CIDR ranges and peering checklist. We support private VPC peering (no public IPs required) and will supply NAT/egress guidance.

SLOs
- Availability: 99.9% for the reserved baseline pool (excludes scheduled maintenance)
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for the sample 512-token profile during steady-state testing (we'll capture metrics in the console)

Action items updated:
- Redwood to provision reserved 2x A100 for baseline (provisioning will begin after your confirmation)
- Autoscale soft-cap at 4, hard-cap at 6 (emergency bursts)
- We'll target Wed 07/14 10am PT for kickoff once peering is scheduled

Links: SOW (DocSend) - https://docsend.com/view/acme-poc-sow; HubSpot deal - https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-POC-47

Please reply-all to confirm the soft/hard caps and we'll start the provisioning ticket.

Best,
Marissa
